title: config-delta-safety-layer-with-weighted-hypothesis-canary-and-auto-recovery
creator: Priya Singh
description:
Background: Recent incidents show regressions happen not only from model weights but also subtle config deltas (tokenization, sampling params, kv-cache flags). Current canary AB guards use fixed traffic slices and single-threshold checks which miss correlated small shifts across multiple metrics. Goal: ship a lightweight safety layer that computes a config-delta-aware hypothesis score, drives weighted traffic ramps, and triggers an explainable automatic recovery (rollback or degrade) when the hypothesis crosses calibrated risk bounds.

Scope: build the config delta snapshotter, hypothesis scoring service (aggregate metric drift, weighted failure modes), a traffic policy engine that uses weighted ramps (e.g., 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% with hold windows), and an auto-recovery controller that executes one of: immediate rollback, degrade to fallback model, or isolate cohort. Integrate with existing eval probes, synthetic checks, and console runbooks.

Design notes: hypothesis score is a linear combination of standardized metric deltas (quality metrics, hallucination rate, latency, token-cost delta), with per-customer weights inferred from historical sensitivity. We keep a short-term baseline window (T-72h) and snapshot pre-change config. Hysteresis and hold windows avoid flapping: require two successive evaluation windows exceeding upper bound or a single window exceeding catastrophic threshold. All decisions must produce an explainable rationale (metric deltas + contributing config keys) recorded to audit logs.

Acceptance criteria: (1) can detect injected synthetic regressions in test harness with >95% precision and <10% false-positive rate; (2) can perform an automated rollback in staging and record playbook steps to the console; (3) end-to-end latency impact < 2% for steady-state traffic; (4) dashboards expose the hypothesis score, contributing metric breakdown, and rollback transcripts.

Out of scope: full cohort-level A/B experimentation UI — this is a safety layer that plugs into existing rollout flows and the rollout service will consume decisions via a documented API.
comments: 2026-02-28 - Initial ticket created after postmortem for REG-2026-02: model-config drift led to increased hallucination in payments flow. Hypothesis: multiple small tokenization and sampling changes combined to produce the regression.

2026-03-02 - Design review with PM/RE: agreed on weighted hypothesis scoring, need to prototype snapshot format and baseline window length. Action: Marco to prototype snapshotter; Aisha to draft eval metrics list.

2026-03-05 - Prototype complete: snapshotter captures config keys, normalized metric deltas. Early tests show hypothesis scores correlate with injected perturbations (precision 0.9). Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-safety/pull/438

2026-03-08 - Architecture review notes: ensure audit log entries include provenance (commit id, deploy id, baseline window). Add synthetic probe for tokenization regressions. Security flagged requirement for encryption-in-transit for snapshot payloads (see security review).

2026-03-12 - Integration work started with rollout-controller: traffic policy API v0.2 implemented. Added console telemetry panels prototype: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/rollout-safety/hypothesis-score
Follow-ups: expose per-customer weight overrides, add TTL for snapshots, and run chaos test against autoscaler to validate no unintended rollbacks under load.
